episodes.181851: A line of thunderstorms produced strong winds in a few locations during the early morning hours. A tree was knocked down in Madison County, blocking a road, and resulted in a vehicle running into it.
episodes.182578: A stalled frontal boundary was the focus for storms that produced lightning that caused a church fire in Barnwell.
episodes.182633: A cold front brought the threat of severe thunderstorms to northeast South Dakota on the afternoon and evening of August 10th. Initially, individual storms presented both a hail and wind threat in the James Valley, with reports of golfball sized hail in Brown and Hand counties. As the storms moved east into the Prairie Coteau region, they organized into a broken line and presented more of a wind threat. The Department of Transportation mesonet station 6 miles west of Henry recorded a 74 mph wind gust, and the nearby town of Henry also experienced damage to trees. There was also a pair of brief tornado touchdowns farther to the south associated with one of the stronger cells embedded within this line, though no damage was ever noted.
episodes.182658: After heavy rainfall during the first half of August, the James river gauge at Ashton rose above flood stage on the morning of August 11th and remained in flood through August 21st. The river crested at 13.25 on August 18th, 0.25 feet above flood stage. This only impacted already previously flooded crop and pastures.
episodes.183052: A supercell thunderstorm produced a swath of severe weather across portions of south central Nebraska during the evening of August 10th. A weak upper level disturbance and associated surface front/trough sparked isolated thunderstorms in Dawson and Buffalo Counties between 4-5 PM CDT. These storms developed amidst warm surface temperatures (near 90 degrees) and strong instability (CAPE values near 2000 J/kg). The strong instability and adequate deep layer shear allowed the isolated storms to morph into a singular, dominant supercell that tracked from the Kearney area at around 5 PM, southeastward towards Superior by around 9 PM. Large hail was the primary severe threat, with several instances of significant severe hail (at least 2 inches in diameter) reported along its path. As a result, the main impact from this severe event was crop damage, though vehicle and home damage also occurred. The storm exited Nebraska altogether between 9-10 PM CDT.
episodes.183370: Thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front and shortwave across Minnesota during the afternoon hours on Friday (8/11).  These storms tracked east through Wisconsin during the evening hours.  The strongest storms produced damaging winds and hail up to tennis ball size.
episodes.183609: Thunderstorms developed overnight across Iowa, ahead of a cold front, in an environment characterized by moderate instability and shear. The storms congealed into a line that swept across central Illinois during the early morning hours of August 11, producing scattered damaging winds before weakening after moving east of I-55. The thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall over 1 inch, which led to minor flooding in urban areas.
episodes.183701: Dangerously high heat index values combined with forcing from a passing mid-level short wave trough and approaching surface front triggered late day severe storms across SE GA.
episodes.184033: A supercell developed in Saline County and produced 1-to-2-inch diameter hail in a consistent line across 3 counties in the early afternoon on August 11.
episodes.184142: A strong storm system and associated cold front moved around the periphery of a high pressure system situated over the Gulf of Mexico. The boundary triggered scattered severe thunderstorms in northern Arkansas during the night-time hours bringing to large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
episodes.184428: Scattered strong to severe (high-based) thunderstorms moved from central Texas into portions of western-north Texas, aided by regeneration along convective cold pools/outflow, on the evening of the 10th. While a few reports of sub-severe hail were received initially, storm organization increased towards the Wichita Falls Metropolitan area. A significant and damaging microburst event occurred from the western to central portions of the city. The most significant damage occurred in the vicinity of Loop 11 and Seymour Highway, where a large section of a strip mall was destroyed. Additional significant damage to buildings and residences occurred sporadically along Seymour Highway (towards Interstate 44). Wind speeds as high as 100-110 mph may have been realized across these areas. Widespread tree and power line damage was also noted across the aforementioned areas.
episodes.184429: Scattered high-based convection moved from the eastern Texas Panhandle into portions of western and central Oklahoma on the evening of the 11th. Amidst significant downdraft potential energy, scattered damaging wind events (some significant) were noted across the previously mentioned areas.
episodes.184508: A disturbance moved across the area during the early morning hours of August 11th, resulting in a line of showers and thunderstorms that moved eastward across the area. One these storms become severe in Mercer County, near the town of Hamlet, where thunderstorm wind gusts brought 2 to 3 inch tree branches down.
episodes.184525: A line of severe storms moved through southeast Minnesota during the evening of August 11th and produced winds in excess of 60 mph as well as quarter sized hail near Rochester (Olmsted County). Broadcast media reported power outages in the City of Winona (Winona County) and Claremont (Dodge County) from fallen trees on power lines.
episodes.184526: A line of severe storms moved through western and central Wisconsin during evening of August 11th, resulting in coinciding corridors of severe reports. In western Wisconsin, volunteer observers reported toppled trees and power lines from severe wind gusts from Buffalo to Richland County. Highest wind gusts included an estimated 80 mph from a NWS storm survey of extensive damage in Westby (Vernon County) and a measured gust of 68 mph in the city of La Crosse (La Crosse County) by an automated weather observation station. In central Wisconsin, volunteer observers reported 60 mph wind gusts and quarter inch hail near Loyal (Clark County).
episodes.184528: Numerous showers and thunderstorms filtered in across portions of Southeast Michigan through the evening of August 11, 2023. The strongest storms were found within the vicinity of or along a warm front, which produced sporadic reports of hail up to an inch and some isolated damaging wind gusts. Prolonged heavy rainfall also led to flooding within Flint which led to multiple road closures. The most significant damage came from a supercell over Perry, MI, which resulted in the production of an EF-1 tornado with maximum wind gusts up to 95 mph. This tornado was on the ground for 12 minutes and started just west of Perry, before moving into the city. Uprooted and sheared trees, damage to outbuildings, and some siding/shingle damage to residential builds were observed. Downed trees also landed on some residential houses and vehicles, resulting in further damage.
episodes.184604: An isolated severe storm developed across western Nebraska and moved across the southern Sandhills with damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.184626: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184633: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184693: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.184730: An occluded low pressure system moved across the Upper Midwest during the afternoon and evening hours of the 11th. Storms formed in the warm sector ahead of the cold front south of a triple-point that moved through the Brainerd area. These storms were mainly wind-producing storms with multiple reports of tree damage received from the Brainerd Lakes area eastward into the I-35 corridor.
episodes.184731: An occluded low pressure system moved across the Upper Midwest during the afternoon and evening hours of the 11th. Storms formed in the warm sector ahead of the cold front south of a triple-point that moved through the Brainerd area to near the Twin Ports. A few storms led to some minor tree damage and marginally severe hail in Burnett County as they moved through northwestern Wisconsin.
episodes.184735: A series of short-wave troughs moved through the area and interacted with elevated instability and marginal deep layer shear to produce a thunderstorm over far northwest North Dakota. The storm moved southeast into Ward County where it became severe, producing one-inch diameter hail and wind gusts to 71 mph at the Minot Air Force Base. The storm continued to move southeast, producing sub-severe hail over McHenry and McLean counties.
episodes.184738: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Cache River at Patterson August 11-21, 2023.
episodes.184751: Fast moving squall line affected most of northeast SC. The line was strongest in Georgetown and across the Grand Strand. Shortly after encountering the sea breeze the convection began to weaken as the outflow moved ahead of the line.
episodes.184752: A fast moving squall line affected most of northeast SC. The line was strongest in Georgetown and across portions of the Grand Strand. Shortly after encountering the sea breeze the convection began to weaken as the outflow moved ahead of the line.
episodes.184754: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of east central and southeastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 11th, to the north of a warm front that was near the Red River. The strongest storms produced large hail in excess of two inches in diameter. ||The warm front translated northward during the day of the 11th, with another round of thunderstorms developing during the early evening hours across northeastern Oklahoma. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184934: The remnants of Eastern Pacific Tropical Storm Eugene fueled scattered thunderstorms over southeast California. A few produced flash flooding and strong winds.
episodes.184950: A surface low pressure center and a weak frontal boundary kicked off isolated thunderstorms across western and central portions of North Texas on the afternoons and evenings of August 9 & 10. Wind damage and large hail occurred in a few of these storms.
episodes.184991: A shortwave and warm air advection sparked off convection in southeastern North Dakota in the evening hours of August 10th. Large hail was reported from these storms.
episodes.184993: Discrete severe storms moved through west-central Minnesota on August 11th, with large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185023: Scattered thunderstorms developed across southeast West Tennessee within an axis of very unstable air. There was enough wind shear aloft for some storm organization. An isolated storm over Hardeman became severe with damaging winds.
episodes.185042: A cluster of thunderstorms ongoing across parts of central Georgia was forced eastward by a shortwave, encountering moderate levels of surface-based CAPE, strong low-level lapse rates, high levels of downdraft CAPE and moderate levels of 0-6 km bulk shear across southeast South Carolina. As a result, a few thunderstorms became strong to severe with damaging winds.
episodes.185043: A cluster of thunderstorms ongoing across parts of central Georgia was forced eastward by a shortwave across the local area, encountering moderate levels of surface-based CAPE, strong low-level lapse rates, high levels of downdraft CAPE and moderate levels of 0-6 km bulk shear. As a result, a few thunderstorms became strong to severe with damaging winds, eventually shifting offshore and tracking across coastal waters.
episodes.185050: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of the Big Country during the late afternoon and evening of August 9th and across portions of the Big Country and the Concho Valley during late afternoon and evening of August 10th. A few storms were severe and produced wind damage.
episodes.185124: A continued pattern of westerly or northwesterly upper level flow produced several consecutive days of severe weather across northeastern and southeastern portions of Central Alabama.
episodes.185126: A line of thunderstorms moved through the region during the late evening of August 10, 2023. These storms generally produced wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph, but a few locally higher gusts were observed, as well as some tree and powerline damage.
episodes.185127: On August 11, 2023 an unstable air mass with ample deep layer shear supported numerous supercell thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. These storms produced widespread large hail, along with some damaging wind. A few reports were for greater than 2 inch hail. This event was categorized as a billion dollar disaster in Minnesota by the National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI).
episodes.185128: On August 11, 2023 an unstable air mass with ample deep layer shear supported numerous supercell thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. These storms produced widespread large hail, along with some damaging wind. A few reports were for greater than 2 inch hail.
episodes.185224: An isolated supercell produced hail in Republic County during the evening of 8/10.
episodes.185271: A late day frontal zone moved into an unstable airmass with up to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE and sparked several severe thunderstorms, which produced large hail up to golf ball size. In addition, a couple of brief tornadic spin ups occurred across Kingsbury County, but resulted in no damage.
episodes.185275: With a lingering upper-level trough across the area, a weak surface convergence axis and diurnal destabilization produced a few late afternoon thunderstorms across southwest Minnesota and into northwest Iowa in the evening. Stronger cells produced marginally large hail, and some damaging wind gusts with a strong sub-cloud dry layer.
episodes.185291: An upper level shortwave traveling across the region, paired with modest MUCAPE and moisture above the midlevels allowed for sub-severe to severe hail across portions of Northern Iowa through the late evening. Large hail of 2-3 inches occurred in Humboldt and Hancock counties with these storms.
episodes.186587: Several gale-force peak convective wind gusts impacted the OH and PA shore of Lake Erie on August 6th and 10th. During the early afternoon through early evening of the 6th, a surface low drifted northeastward from northwestern OH to Lake St. Clair. The low became occluded as the trailing cold front moved eastward from far-western OH to central OH and a nearly-stationary front lingered near the Lake Erie shore in north-central and northeast OH. Isolated to scattered multicell thunderstorms persisted generally northeastward across far-northern OH and Lake Erie during the late afternoon through early evening after developing along the occluded and nearly-stationary fronts. These storms occurred along a tight gradient of MUCAPE and in a region of weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear.  ||Several days later, a cold front drifted generally southward across southern ON and southern Lower MI to northern Lake Erie during the early afternoon through early evening of the 10th. Isolated to scattered multicell showers and thunderstorms persisted generally southeastward across Lake Erie after developing along the front. The storms persisted amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.

Damage located around the intersection of Polly St and Lamb St and southeast into the intersection of 2nd St and Washington St consisted of large uprooted trees, sheared large tree limbs, major roofing damage to several outbuildings, and shingle/siding damaging to some residential homes. These locations observed a peak wind around 95 mph with a tornado width around 430 yards.
